contract_term.value: Up to five years of optional Load Ramp plus a twelve-year Term (held); the Term begins on the date permanent service begins or as the LLCS Service Agreement sets out; automatic five-year Extension Terms unless either party gives at least 36 months' written notice before the end of the Term or Extension Term; termination before the end of the Term needs a Termination Notice at least 24 months before the Termination Date

cites.quote: The Term shall commence on the date permanent service begins, or as set forth in the LLCS Service Agreement.

the LLCS Service Agreement will automatically extend for periods of five years ("Extension Term") at the end of the Term or any Extension Term, unless either party to the LLCS Service Agreement provides at least thirty-six (36) months' written notice to the other party prior to the end of the Term or any Extension Term

the customer must deliver a written notice (a "Termination Notice") to Ameren Missouri not less than twenty-four (24) months prior to the effective date of the termination specified in the Termination Notice

collateral.value: Two years of Minimum Monthly Bills (held); a customer that, with any Guarantor, meets credit rating and liquidity tests is exempt from 60, 50, 40 or 25 percent of it, those discounts capped at $175 million, $150 million, $125 million and $75 million; provided at the time of executing the LLCS Service Agreement; the Company considers reductions annually once the customer has been at peak load for at least three years

cites.quote: will be exempt from sixty (60) percent of the Collateral Requirement, with the sixty (60) percent discount not to exceed $175 million

after the customer has achieved their peak load for at least three (3) years, annually consider reducing the customer's collateral obligation

exit_fee.value: Exit Fee during and after the Ramp Period (held); in addition an Early Termination Fee of two times the Minimum Monthly Bill times the months short of the 24 months' notice; capacity may be cut by up to 20 percent in total without charge on 24 months' notice, and beyond that after the first five years of the Term on 24 months' notice subject to a Capacity Reduction Fee

cites.quote: An additional fee shall apply if the customer seeks to terminate with less than twenty-four (24)-months' notice (the "Early Termination Fee").
the applicable Minimum Monthly Bill times the number of months less than the twenty-four (24)-months' notice required for termination.

by up to twenty (20) percent of the Contract Capacity ("Permissible Capacity Reduction"), in total, without charge for such reduction. To do so, the customer must provide the Company at least twenty-four (24)-months' prior written notice.

with the effective date of any such reduction occurring at any time after the first five (5) years of the Term by giving the Company at least twenty-four (24) months' written notice prior to the beginning of the year for which the reduction is sought, subject to payment of a Capacity Reduction Fee.

rows.notes: Sheet 61.13 (p. 12) adds an Interim Capacity Adjustment: if the existing system cannot serve the load, the Company may buy market capacity under an Interim Capacity Agreement at the customer's full cost. Missouri S.B. 4 (2025): the Missouri PSC's fact sheet says the law required the PSC to adopt rates for large load customers and that Ameren Missouri and Evergy have approved large-load tariffs (https://psc.mo.gov/CMSInternetData/Community%20Outreach/Large%20Load%20Tariff%20Fact%20Sheet.pdf, p. 1); the tariff sheets themselves do not cite the law. The 2026 preferred resource plan (Ameren 10-Q, same section) forecasts total load growth of 2.9 GW by 2030, 5 GW by 2035 and 6 GW by 2045: a forecast, not a queue. Leads only (news summaries of Ameren's earnings calls, not read): 3.4 GW of construction agreements in Missouri and a further 4 GW of Missouri projects with completed interconnection studies (Q2 2026 call); Ameren's posted call transcript on s21.q4cdn.com was refused (robots answered 403). ameren.com was not read: its terms forbid bots and automated tools (see refused), so the queue details the Company posts on its website (Sheet 126) are unread. The Order Approving Tariff Revision of 19 December 2025 (EFIS 860789) was not read.

threshold_mw.value: 75 MW: a new customer with a peak load of 75 MW or greater, or an existing customer expanding by 75 MW or greater

cites.quote: The rate would apply to any new customer with a peak load of 75 MW or greater, or an existing customer with an expansion of 75 MW or greater.
The new LLPS rates will apply to any new facility beginning service with a peak load forecast at 75 megawatts (75 MW) or more, or an existing customer expecting to expand by 75 MW.

min_demand.value: Minimum monthly bill based on 80 percent of contract demand, whatever the actual usage

cites.quote: Customers pay a minimum monthly bill that is based on 80% of their contract demand, regardless of their actual monthly usage.

contract_term.value: 12 years plus an optional load ramp of up to five years (up to 17 years in all); then automatic five-year extensions

cites.quote: Customers will be required to sign a 12-year contract, plus an optional load ramp period of up to five years, for a total contract length of up to
17-years. Thereafter, the contract automatically extends for five years at a time.

collateral.value: Two years of Minimum Monthly Bills, as calculated by Evergy, under creditworthiness standards

cites.quote: Schedule LLPS customers are required to provide collateral in an amount equal to two (2) years of Minimum Monthly Bills, as calculated by Evergy.
Collateral requirements of up to 2 years of Minimum Bills.

exit_fee.value: 36 months' advance notice to terminate early, and an exit fee of the Minimum Monthly Bill times the months remaining in the term, or 12 months, whichever is greater; with less than 36 months' notice, the exit fee plus two times the Minimum Monthly Bill times the months short of 36. Capacity may be reduced by the lower of 25 MW or 10 percent of contract capacity

cites.quote: If the customer terminates service early, they are required to provide 36-months advance notice, and pay an exit fee equal to the nominal value of the minimum monthly bill times the number of months remaining in the contract term, or 12-months, whichever is greater.
the Exit Fee plus two (2) times the nominal value of the Minimum Monthly Bill times the number of months less than the thirty-six (36) months' notice required for termination.
Customers taking LLPS service can reduce their service under the tariff rate by 25 MW or up to 10 percent of the total capacity of the contract, whichever is lower.
